headlines.title: Adobe stock: Here are 5 strategic questions into new leadership
headlines.summary: Investing.com -- Goldman Sachs maintained its “sell” rating on Adobe as Anil Chakravarthy prepares to take over as president and CEO on Dec. 1, saying competition is intensifying and new entrants are gaining ground in areas that could expand Adobe’s market.

headlines.title: How Investors Are Reacting To Adobe (ADBE) Expanding AI CX With NHL And Jet2 Partnerships
headlines.summary: In late September 2026, Adobe and the National Hockey League announced a partnership making Adobe the League’s Official Creative, Marketing and AI Partner, while Adobe also revealed a multi-year AI-powered customer experience collaboration with Jet2 to personalise holiday planning and travel content. Together, these alliances put Adobe’s CX Enterprise, Firefly and GenStudio tools at the centre of large-scale, real-world customer engagement programs across sport and travel.

headlines.title: Adobe Still Has $24.5 Billion Left for Buybacks. That's About a Quarter of the Company.
headlines.summary: At its current pace, the software giant could spend it all before 2030. What might that do to earnings per share?

headlines.title: Adobe Forecasts 130% Surge in AI-Driven Retail Traffic During US Holiday Season
headlines.summary: Adobe forecasts that traffic from artificial intelligence tools to US retail websites will increase 130% during the upcoming holiday shopping season, exceeding expected growth from paid search and social media referrals. AI-referred traffic is projected to rise 159% year over year on Thanksgiving, 95% on Black Friday and 88% on Cyber Monday, according to Adobe.

headlines.title: The Adobe Stock Debate Is About to Get Interesting
headlines.summary: Adobe beat earnings for the fifth straight quarter, yet the stock sits 31% in the hole for the year while a generative AI rival just torched its retail sentiment. Something has to give, and the answer depends on a bet most investors are getting wrong.

description: Adobe Inc. operates as a technology company worldwide. The Digital Media segment offers products and services that enable individuals, teams, and enterprises to create, publish, and promote content. This segment serves photographers, video editors, graphic and experience designers, game developers, content creators, students, marketers, business owners, knowledge workers, and consumers. The Digital Experience segment provides an integrated platform; and products, services, and solutions that enable brands and businesses to create, manage, execute, measure, monetize, and optimize customer experiences from analytics to commerce. This segment serves marketers, advertisers, agencies, publishers, merchandisers, merchants, web analysts, data scientists, developers, and executives across the C-suite. The Publishing and Advertising segment offers e-learning, technical document publishing, web conferencing, document and forms platform, web application development, printing, and Adobe Advertising solutions. It also provides consulting, training, customer management, technical support, and learning services. The company offers its solutions to enterprise customers, and businesses and consumers; and licenses its products to end-user customers through app stores and website at adobe.com. It markets and distributes its products through distributors, retailers, software developers, mobile app stores, systems integrators, independent software vendors, value-added resellers, and original equipment and hardware manufacturers. The company also provides an online visibility management and content marketing software-as-a-service platform. The company has a strategic alliance with HUMAIN for the development of generative AI models and AI-powered applications. The company was formerly known as Adobe Systems Incorporated and changed its name to Adobe Inc. in October 2018. Adobe Inc. was founded in 1982 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.
